_note: The cash bar: "Any deduction for a donation over ₹ 2000 shall be allowed only if the payment is made by a mode other than cash" (s.133(5), p.169) — per donation; one over the limit in cash is allowed nothing, one within it is allowed as any other. A definition (CashPaymentLimit), not a cap, because the excess is not what is disallowed. Old regime only: s.202(2)(a)(xii) excludes Chapter VIII other than ss.124(1), 124(2), 125(2) and 146 (p.227). TY 2026-27 and TY 2025-26; the 1961 counterpart, s.80G, is the TY 2025-26 version (W-075d5). rulebook DED-80G-001. D-142. TY 2025-26: Income-tax Act, 1961 s.80G(5D) (thc p.353): "No deduction shall be allowed under this section in respect of donation of any sum exceeding two thousand rupees unless such sum is paid by any mode other than cash"; Explanation 5: only a sum of money. The same definition. sources/2026-10-07-chapter-via.md B27. D-148. In every regime as a row; the new regime forbids it through DIS-NEW-TAX-REGIME-NO-EXEMPTION, whose basis REG-NEW-TAX-REGIME-NO-EXEMPTION (S2 s.202(2)(a); 1961 s.115BAC(2)(i)) every explanation cites (D-166).

introducedBy.instrumentCitation: Income-tax Act, 1961 (43 of 1961), s.80G(5D) — "two thousand rupees" subs. by Act 7 of 2017, s.35 (w.e.f. 1-4-2018)
